lines.text: An interview is like a football match. You can't win without training. Ready?
Ready.
Step one: research. Learn about the company. Read their website. What do they do? What are their goals?
Research. Got it.

Step two: practice. Some questions come in almost every interview. "Tell me about yourself." "Why do you want this job?" "How do you handle stress?" Prepare your answers. Then record yourself and listen.
Record myself? That's weird.
Weird, but it works. You'll hear every "um" and every "like."
Step three: listen. Listen to the whole question. Then pause, think, and answer. It's OK to say, "That's a good question. Let me think."
Step four: be professional. Wear a suit. Arrive early. Smile and make eye contact.
Research, practice, listen, be professional. I can do this.
Tell me about yourself… Hi, I'm Adam. Um… no. Again.
Who are you talking to?
Myself. It's Sami's idea.
Can I be the interviewer?
Please!
Mr. Fares, how do you handle stress?
That's a good question. When I feel stressed, I stay calm and focus on one problem at a time.
Wow! Who are you, and what did you do with my brother?
You're up early again?
English podcast. Every morning, I listen and repeat. And I finished an online course in customer service. Look, a certificate!
I'm proud of you, son.
Mom, look! BlueLine has a new job ad. Same company. Same job.
So what are you waiting for?

questions.a: Example: I feel a little shy, but I'm happy because I'm speaking English.
